# `state/util/canonical.js`

> **Source:** `engine/state/util/canonical.js`

state/util/canonical.js — deterministic serialization + self-describing, algorithm-tagged hash IDs (CSE Integrity plane, spec §13).  Equivalent data MUST produce byte-identical bytes before hashing or signing (spec rule 58). We implement an RFC 8785-style canonical JSON: object keys are sorted by UTF-16 code unit, arrays keep order, no insignificant whitespace, and non-finite numbers are rejected. Hash IDs are multihash-style (`alg:bits:hex`) so the algorithm can migrate later (spec rule 59).  Two tiers, matching the engine's hybrid integrity policy: • hot-path id   — synchronous 32-bit FNV (runtime identity / state roots). • authority id  — async Web Crypto SHA-256 (capabilities, receipts, checkpoints) where security matters.

## Functions

### `canonicalize(value)`

Produce a deterministic canonical JSON string for any JSON-compatible value. Object keys are sorted; Maps and Sets are normalized; arrays preserve order.

**Parameters:**

- `value` *(*)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

### `canonicalBytes(value, { domain = DOMAIN_SEPARATOR, schemaVersion = '' } = {})`

Domain-separated canonical bytes string used as hash/sign input (spec §13).

### `hashIdFast(value, opts = {})`

Synchronous hot-path id: 32-bit FNV over canonical bytes. Tagged so it is self-describing and migratable. Fast, NOT collision-resistant — identity for runtime state, never a security claim (spec rule 52).

**Returns:** `fnv1a32:32:<hex8>`

### `async hashIdSecure(value, opts = {})`

Async authority id: Web Crypto SHA-256 over canonical bytes. Use for capabilities, witness receipts, checkpoints, and signed transactions. Throws if SubtleCrypto is unavailable (callers degrade explicitly).

**Returns:** `sha256:256:<hex64>`

### `parseHashId(id)`

Parse a tagged hash id into `{ alg, bits, hex }` or null.

### `hashIdEquals(a, b)`

True when two tagged hash ids are byte-equal (same algorithm + digest).

## Constants

- `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR` — Domain separator prefix so hashes of different structures never collide.
